          DEFCONs, Set Pieces, Budget Picks, Wildcards? Six Key FPL Questions Ahead of GW6
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      Dan Edwards / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
The international break has given Fantasy Premier League managers plenty to think about. Using Opta data and Solio's projections, we assess six of the biggest questions ahead of GW6, including fixture difficulty, defensive contribution points, budget forwards and whether it's too late to jump on Pascal Groß.

Brentford’s 3-0 dismantling of Chelsea, Brighton’s shock undoing of Arsenal by the same scoreline, and Brian Brobbey’s Etihad Stadium hat-trick all feel like a lifetime ago, but in Fantasy Premier League terms, they occurred only last week.

After the longest international break on record, you’d be forgiven for forgetting the contents of your Fantasy Premier League squad, but it’s time to get your head back in the game, because a lot has happened – on and off the field.

To help you get back in business, we’ve combined Opta data with Solio FPL’s projections to answer six common questions Fantasy managers are likely to have after looking at their squads following the long break.
If you want to skip ahead to a certain question, just click on it.
The introduction of defensive contribution points in Fantasy Premier League ahead of the 2025-26 season was arguably the most seismic change ever made to the format.

Defenders now earn two additional points by combining for at least 10 tackles, interceptions, clearances, and blocks in a single game. The threshold for midfielders and forwards was set at 12, but recoveries also counted towards their total.

While Elliot Anderson and Marcos Senesi, for example, may have previously had limited Fantasy relevance, players of their profile were suddenly thrust into the spotlight, expanding the practical player pool as a result.

Having started 2025-26 priced at £5.5m, Anderson ended up as the game’s fifth-highest-scoring midfielder, largely as a result of his league-leading 52 points from defensive contributions. To put this into context, a forward has to score 13 goals to earn 52 points.

It was a similar story for Senesi, who ranked third among defenders last season for total points despite being priced at £4.5m on the opening day. He earned 50 points from defensive contributions, second only to Anderson.

The impact of defensive contributions was perhaps greater than initially anticipated. In 2024-25, the season prior, players would have reached the threshold for defensive contribution points in 16.8% of their starts on average. That hit rate rose sharply to 19.3% in 2025-26, a figure which saw this method of points-scoring become a necessary focus.

But are defensive contributions as important this season as they were last? It’s debatable. The hit rate five rounds into this season is 16.9%, seemingly falling back in line with the season before last – but that number doesn’t tell the whole story.

In each of the previous three seasons, the hit rate after five rounds has been lower than at the season’s culmination. Indeed, this season’s figure is actually higher than it was at the same point last season (16.7%).

The tendency for DEFCON hit rates to increase as the season progresses is especially evident among defenders. Looking at the last three seasons, comparing figures after GW5 with end-of-season totals, defenders' DEFCON hit rates increased by an average of 10.3% over the course of the campaign.
This could be for myriad reasons. Perhaps systems become more distinct, games become more consequential, and players become more desperate towards the end of the season.
Either way, there is enough evidence to suggest it’s an element of the game which could become more and more important as the season progresses.

If this is the case, which players should Fantasy managers be targeting? The leaders for points earned via defensive contributions this season are Kobbie Mainoo, António Silva and Murillo, with eight each. Mainoo has reached the threshold in all four of his starts.
Solio’s projections page gives us an insight into which players are likely to prosper in the near future, and you can even look at a player’s chance of reaching the threshold on a game-by-game level.

Kevin Danso and Tarik Muharemovic lead Solio’s projections with an average hit rate of 64% across the next six games, with both players noticeably clear of any teammate. By way of comparison, Senesi reached the threshold in 70% of his appearances last season.

Anderson is the highest-ranking midfielder by this measure using Solio’s projections, with a forecasted average hit rate of 51% over the next six gameweeks. Meanwhile, Exequiel Palacios’ projected hit rate of 47% makes him a noticeable outlier among midfielders at his price point (£5.0m).
